classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that everyone belongs to the union, recover the overlap and combine the exclusive regions.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by drawing a Venn diagram.

Two hundred and forty university students take part in a demonstration, all of them are either carrying banners or sitting down on the road or both. Eighty-four carry banners and 204 sit on the road. Find how many students:

children.label: a
children.prompt: sit down on the road and carry banners

answer.short:
48 students.

All 240 students belong to the union, so subtract 240 from the sum of the two set totals.
answer.worked:
Let $B$ represent carrying banners and $S$ sitting on the road. Everyone is in $B\cup S$, so $|B\cup S|=240$ and the outside region is 0.
$$\begin{align*}|B\cap S|&=84+204-240\\|B\cap S|&=48\end{align*}$$
Put 48 in the overlap.

children.label: b
children.prompt: do only one of these things

answer.worked: The banners-only region contains $84-48=36$ students. The sitting-only region contains $204-48=156$ students. Add these disjoint regions: $36+156=192$ students.

spec.description: Authored answer diagram: B denotes carrying banners and S sitting on the road.
spec.mathematics: Banners only 36; both 48; sitting only 156; neither 0.
